findings: Open zine is a pair of joined shallow page planes with closed thickness, nested cover/paper layers and a shared central crease. Six views show complete V-shaped front/rear edges and plausible depth ordering.

Collage and line motifs use sheet-local coordinates, so they remain attached to the page when projected from any camera. Two staple crowns span the spine and their short legs penetrate the nested sheets.
Pencil is a connected collinear lead, wood taper, hexagonal barrel, ferrule and eraser. A whole-object translation keeps it outside the booklet silhouette, exposing the making cue at24/32px.
Dimensions, paper curvature and drawn page graphics are illustrative. Staples soften below32px. This is not an exhaustive collision test or a bookbinding instruction diagram.

Poetry-writing, speed-dating, clothing-swap and theater-screening are original planar emblems. Shirt arrows have opposite destinations; mask faces are conventional flat symbols, not modeled human anatomy.

references.finding: NYPL describes zines as diverse handmade magazines, including handwritten, photocopied and stapled examples.
CUNY library making guide treats stapled booklet construction as one zine format.
